svg.text: GA-03 Stand-and-fill rack: the fixture goes to the table
An open shell cannot be held by a hand that is not there — so a bent-sheet rack holds it and is served with it.
tacos MX02, hot dog US02, gyros ME03
no actuator · washed with the dishes
Soft taco: the tortilla sags into the trough
end view, 2 px per mm · the rack is served on the plate
Crisp shells: bake on the inverted rack
home method, 8 min at 180 °C · no fragile bought shells
W-rack: 1 mm bent stainless sheet, troughs 45 wide × 60 deep × 160 long

g.text: warm tortilla laid on by the peel (GA-01), sags in by its own weight

svg.text: same rack holds a hot-dog bun (a V-plough opens the slit),
a folded pita for gyros, a finished wrap seam-up
camera: fill line · load cell: quantity · conf. H
inverted, the W is an M: tortillas draped over the ridges

g.text: a rod across the top holds them in the fan air
second rack clamped on, pair inverted: shells mouth-up

svg.text: bought hard shells come nested and break at 5–10 N:
conf. H soft tortilla and hot dog, M baked shells

g.text: 1/5 A warm soft tortilla is laid over a trough of the W-rack by the peel.
2/5 It sags into the trough under its own weight — the rack holds the open shell.
3/5 The depositors pass above: meat, cheese, lettuce, sauce, each by mass.
4/5 Crisp shells: the rack turned over is a bake form; tortillas are draped over the ridges and baked.
5/5 A second rack is clamped on and the pair inverted: the shells now stand mouth-up, ready to fill.
